_note: Phase 34.5 — the client-facing register of every adjustable input. It DOCUMENTS the engine and never contradicts it: each row with an `engine_binding` is asserted equal to the value the code actually holds (see register.mjs + __tests__/register.test.ts), so the register cannot drift from the model. Values are the canonical ones pulled FROM the engine/configs, never re-typed alongside them (discipline rule #4).
_override_mechanism: `override` is the Prosperus-adjustable handle. When non-null the runner uses it in place of `value`; `value` is never overwritten, so the engine-derived figure and the client's edit stay side by side and the delta is always visible.
_value_basis: Rows marked `basis: "live-kv"` carry a market observation rather than a modelling choice, synced from the frozen KV fixture so the binding tests gate code rather than detect overnight market movement. The delivery run refreshes them from the KV that produced the client numbers.
_superseded_rows: Rows marked `basis: "superseded"` record a value the model USED to hold, kept beside the value that replaced it. They are provenance, not inputs: nothing reads them, they carry no engine_binding and no override, and each names the row that superseded it and the date. Every other row is bound to live code and asserted equal to it. Those are the only two kinds of row there are.
_sensitivity_range: The plausible band for the assumption, for the tornado/sensitivity view. It is a disclosure of uncertainty, not a hard bound — the scenario driver values are the ones the client locked.
_changelog: Every register value change appends an entry: {date, id, old, new, reason, source, decided_by, phase, register_version}. `decided_by` is a closed vocabulary — operator (a human decision that moves delivered numbers) / measurement (evidence recorded, no value moved) / derived (a consequential re-derivation forced by another change) / governance (a change to the mechanism itself). The six entries dated before 2026-07-29 predate the versioning mechanism and carry register_version null; r1 pins the content as it stood when versioning was introduced. Enforced by validateRegister + __tests__/register.test.ts, not merely documented.
_version: `version.id` is r<seq>.<first 8 hex of a sha256 over every LIVE row's {id, value, override}, sorted by id>. seq counts MODEL changes, not tool invocations. Superseded rows are excluded from the hash because they are provenance, not inputs. validateRegister fails when the stored hash does not describe the current content, so a value cannot move without a bump and bumpVersion refuses a bump with no attributable reason. Every delivered report quotes this id; the changelog up to that version is the set of assumptions the report ran on.

Phase 36.B5: re-based from 678 to 498 EFC/yr when cycle accounting and revenue were put on ONE day-ahead throughput figure (36.B1-O). The metric changed meaning — it was the nameplate anchor plus reserves, it is now DELIVERED throughput (anchor x trading fraction x availability). The observed band that used to be this row's sensitivity_range is retained as benchmark_band: the delivered figure falls below it, which is a reported finding and not a re-fitted band. B1's hourly physical simulation lands lower still (221 EFC/yr). Phase 38.6a: re-based again, 498 to 198 EFC/yr, when the MW partition became the engine default. The day-ahead share the engine spends on MWh moved from `trading_fraction` (0.70, a EUR/EUR price ratio) to the physical MW-hour share `effective_arb_pct` (0.139), so delivered day-ahead throughput fell ~80% and total cycling with it. ladder.basis: the shipped 5pp steps kept and re-anchored on the measurement; both rungs land inside the measured daily distribution (p25 0.628, median 0.756), so stress is 'a year made entirely of bottom-quartile trading days' rather than '20% worse than an assumption'

client_impact_frozen_fixture.note: measured on the frozen KV fixture so the delta is code-attributable in full. The gearing is the story: a 4.5% revenue correction lands as a 16% NPV correction. Stoniskiai's Downside NPV crosses zero (EUR 2 234 571 to -EUR 1 299).

evidence.limitation: ONE market year. The band is an observed range, not a distribution; twelve monthly observations from a single year cannot separate seasonality from trend. Remeasure annually — run-backtest.mjs refuses to adopt a disagreeing remeasurement without a fresh operator decision.

changelog.reason: Consequential, not a decision. The constant closes the engine-vs-client cost-taxonomy gap AT the reference asset's revenue level; adopting the measured trading realisation lowered that revenue, and the engine's two flat cost lines did not follow it down, so the gap widened by EUR 24 245/yr at 50 MW. Re-derived by bridgeCalibration() rather than re-fitted by hand. Without it the reference asset stops closing within the contracted ±2%.
changelog.source: tools/consultancy/bridge.mjs — bridgeCalibration(reference asset, frozen KV fixture)

changelog.reason: ADOPTED. Operator decision 2026-07-28: the measured sub-hourly uplift replaces the Rystad placeholder in RYSTAD_15MIN_UPLIFT_DECIMAL, and the constant gains a register row so it can never again be carried unmeasured. Moves the public dispatch card only — capture_eur_mwh_15min_uplifted falls 4.52% at any capture level; /revenue and every client deliverable number are untouched. Realised-mode card moves only once BTD returns and the cron rewrites dispatch:<date> KV (stored payloads carry the old factor until then, 90-day TTL); forecast-mode computes live but is structurally dead (36.B0-G).

measurement.method: computeDayCapture run at 15 and at 60 minutes on identical days, re-fetched at native resolution (the committed year files are averaged into the hour under decision D1)
measurement.vs_asserted: the Rystad placeholder 0.14 is ~58% higher than measured

reach.revenue_route: unaffected — /revenue 54/54 byte-identical, asserted; the constant is read at exactly two sites, both display fields on the public dispatch card
reach.dispatch_realised: moves only once BTD returns and the ingest cron rewrites dispatch:<date> KV (stored payloads carry the old factor, 90-day TTL)
reach.dispatch_forecast: computes live but the branch is structurally dead (36.B0-G)

evidence.limitation: a display correction, not a model one — no client deliverable number moves.

changelog.reason: Consequential, not a decision. Cycle accounting charged cell wear on the full day-ahead throughput anchor while revenue billed anchor x trading_fraction x availability, so the engine aged the battery for ~43% more day-ahead energy than it earned on (36.B1-O). Both now read one DELIVERED figure. The metric changed basis, so its declared sensitivity_range — the observed merchant-cycling band — was moved to benchmark_band rather than widened to fit: the model now sits below the observed band and says so. cycles_per_day follows at 1.86 -> 1.36.

evidence.cause: 36.B1-O: cycle accounting charged wear on the full day-ahead throughput anchor while revenue billed anchor x trading_fraction x availability, so the engine aged the battery for ~43% more day-ahead energy than it earned on. Closing it by RAISING revenue to the anchor was rejected — it would have added ~43% published revenue and is contradicted by B1's hourly simulation, which finds achieved day-ahead throughput at ~27% of the revenue anchor.
corroboration: 36.B1 hourly chronological simulation, single-year gate: 221 EFC/yr
two independent routes — one a single-year hourly run, one a multi-year fixed point — landing on the same physical answer

declared_breach.treatment: the band keeps its sourced value and the breach is reported at full size and counted in the summary; only the build-failing status is lifted, under expected_deviation with a stated reason. The row's sensitivity_range moved to benchmark_band rather than being widened to contain the new value.

evidence.side_effect: less cycling means slower degradation means higher IRR (+0.9% relative on the reference asset). A consistency fix that improves the answer deserves more scrutiny than one that worsens it, which is why the benchmark consequence was chased rather than accepted quietly.

changelog.reason: The arc endogenous floor is FALSIFIED as written. Gross arbitrage net of cycling cost sits above every floor in the evidence base; found by a reproduction test failing (Baltic aFRR down 17.85 modelled vs 10.04 measured), not by reasoning. A reserve commitment forgoes the SoC headroom it reserves, not the whole MW (36.B1 simultaneity). Displacement is REQUIRED with no default in code — an implicit 1.0 is the assumption being removed. Value shown is Baltic aFRR up; see the sibling rows per product.

changelog.reason: NO PICASSO break parameter, and none should exist. Counted: AT aFRR 0 pre-accession quarter-hours against 54,117; DE aFRR 9 against 226,402. And our own Baltic clearing series starts 2025-10-01, after all three accessions (MARI 2024-10-10; PICASSO Litgrid 2025-03-05, Elering + AST 2025-04-11), so the break is already inside the level the calibration measures. Applying a forward compression would double-count it. Recorded as an explicit NON-APPLICATION so the silence is legible.
